    Mint and redeem

    How minting and redemption works

    Understand how Circle Mint converts fiat to USDC (minting) and USDC back to fiat (redemption), including settlement timing, account structure, and compliance requirements.

    Circle Mint’s core operations are minting and redemption. Minting converts fiat currency into stablecoins (USDC or EURC), and redemption converts stablecoins back to fiat. Every token mints and redeems at a 1:1 ratio with the underlying fiat currency. This page explains the mental model behind these operations, including settlement timing, account structure, onchain transfers, fees, and compliance.

    ​
    Minting

    Minting (also known as an onramp) is the process of depositing fiat currency and receiving an equivalent amount of stablecoins. When you send a fiat transfer to Circle, Circle credits your Mint account balance with the corresponding stablecoin amount at a 1:1 ratio. The minting flow works as follows:
    1. You initiate a fiat transfer from your linked bank account to Circle.
    2. Circle receives the fiat deposit and credits your Mint account balance.
    3. The stablecoins become available for onchain transfers or other operations.
    Circle supports multiple payment rails for fiat deposits, including standard wires (FedWire and SWIFT), real-time interbank rails (RTP, SPEI, SEPA, and CHATS) in supported regions, and book transfers when you bank with one of Circle’s settlement partners. Rail availability depends on your region and the currency you are depositing. Settlement timing: Domestic wire deposits received before the daily cutoff settle on the same business day. Real-time interbank rails settle in seconds, subject to network operating hours and transaction limits. International wires take 1-3 business days depending on intermediary banks. In the sandbox environment, mock wire deposits process in batches and may take up to 15 minutes. For step-by-step instructions, see Deposit Fiat.

    ​
    Redemption

    Redemption (also known as an offramp) is the reverse of minting. You convert stablecoins back to fiat currency by creating a payout to a linked bank account. The redemption flow works as follows:
    1. You create a payout request specifying the amount and destination bank account.
    2. Circle debits the stablecoin amount from your Mint account balance.
    3. Circle sends a fiat transfer to your bank account using the appropriate rail for your region and bank.
    Settlement timing: Payouts typically settle on the next business day. In some cases, your bank may reject the incoming wire, resulting in a returned withdrawal. If a payout is returned, the funds are credited back to your Mint account balance. For step-by-step instructions, see Withdraw Fiat.

    ​
    Account structure

    Your Circle Mint account has several key components that work together to support minting, redemption, and onchain transfers.

    ​
    Primary wallet

    Every Circle Mint account has a primary wallet identified by a masterWalletId. You retrieve this identifier from the /v1/configuration endpoint. The primary wallet serves as the source for outbound transfers and the destination for inbound deposits.

    ​
    Balances

    Your account maintains two types of balances:
    • Available balance: Settled funds you can transfer or redeem immediately.
    • Unsettled balance: Funds that are in transit and not yet available. Wire deposits appear as unsettled until they clear.

    ​
    Linked bank accounts

    You register external bank accounts to send and receive fiat. Each linked bank account receives a unique Virtual Account Number (VAN). When you wire funds to Circle using the VAN, Circle attributes the deposit to your account without requiring a tracking reference in the payment instruction.

    ​
    Deposit addresses

    Circle generates one deposit address per blockchain for your account. These addresses receive inbound stablecoin transfers from external wallets. You retrieve your deposit addresses through the API for each supported blockchain.

    ​
    Recipient addresses

    Recipient addresses are external blockchain addresses that you register and allowlist for outbound transfers. You must create a recipient address before you can send stablecoins to it. This allowlisting step provides an additional layer of security for outbound transfers.

    ​
    Onchain transfers

    Circle Mint supports both receiving and sending stablecoins onchain.
    • Receiving: External wallets send USDC or EURC to your deposit address on any supported blockchain. Circle detects the transfer and credits your account after the required number of blockchain confirmations.
    • Sending: You create a transfer to a registered recipient address. Circle debits your balance and broadcasts the transaction onchain.

    ​
    Transfer status lifecycle

    Onchain transfers progress through the following statuses:
    StatusDescription
    pendingThe transfer request is created but not yet broadcast onchain.
    runningThe transaction is broadcast and awaiting blockchain confirmations.
    completeThe required confirmations are reached and the transfer is final.
    For details on confirmation requirements per blockchain, see Blockchain confirmations. For step-by-step transfer instructions, see Transfer USDC Onchain.

    ​
    Network fees

    Circle covers gas fees for outbound stablecoin transfers in most cases. You do not need to hold the native token of each blockchain to send USDC or EURC from your Mint account.

    ​
    Travel Rule compliance

    Transfers of $3,000 or more in value on supported blockchains are subject to the FinCEN Travel Rule, which requires identity data about the originator of the transaction. How Circle handles the identity requirement depends on the type of transfer:
    • Business account transfers: Circle uses your company’s identity stored on file. You do not need to include identity data in each request.
    • Third-party payouts: If you send funds on behalf of someone else, you must provide the originator’s identity (name and address) in the payout request. Omitting required identity data causes the transfer to fail.
    For the full list of supported blockchains and implementation details, see Travel Rule compliance.

    ​
    Approval workflows

    Customers in France and Singapore are subject to additional recipient address verification requirements. Before an outbound transfer can proceed, the recipient address must be verified through the Mint Console. This approval step ensures compliance with local regulatory requirements in those jurisdictions.

Overview

Lockup is a token distribution protocol that refers to the requirement that the creator of a stream must lock up a certain amount of tokens in a smart contract. A Lockup stream, therefore, is characterized by the start time, end time, amount of tokens to be distributed and a stream shape.

Let's take an example. Imagine Alice wants to stream 3000 DAI to Bob during the whole month of April.

  1. Alice deposits the 3000 DAI in Lockup before Apr 1, setting the end time to May 1.
  2. Bob's allocation of the DAI deposit increases every second beginning Apr 1.
  3. On Apr 10, Bob will have earned approximately 1000 DAI. He can send a transaction to Lockup to withdraw the tokens.
  4. If at any point during April Alice wishes to get back her tokens, she can cancel the stream and recover what has not vested yet.

This distribution model is especially useful for use cases like vesting and airdrops. If you are looking to create an indefinite stream of tokens, please refer to our Flow protocol.

Lockup enables multiple distribution models, a feature that is discussed in the next section.

Setting Up the Contract

This guide is an example of a custodial contract Uniswap v3 positions, which allows interaction with the Uniswap v3 Periphery by minting a position, adding liquidity to a position, decreasing liquidity, and collecting fees.

First, declare the solidity version used to compile the contract and abicoder v2 to allow arbitrary nested arrays and structs to be encoded and decoded in calldata, a feature we use when transacting with a pool.

Import the contracts needed from the npm package installation.

Create a contract called LiquidityExamples and inherit both IERC721Receiver and LiquidityManagement.

We've chosen to hardcode the token contract addresses and pool fee tiers for our example. In production, you would likely use an input parameter for this, allowing you to change the pools and tokens you are interacting with on a per transaction basis.

Declare an immutable public variable nonfungiblePositionManager of type INonfungiblePositionManager.

Allowing ERC721 Interactions

Every NFT is identified by a unique uint256 ID inside the ERC-721 smart contract, declared as the tokenId

To allow deposits of ERC721 expressions of liquidity, create a struct called Deposit, a mapping of uint256 to the Deposit struct, then declare that mapping as a public variable deposits.

The Constructor

Declare the constructor here, which is executed once when the contract is deployed. Our constructor hard codes the address of the nonfungible position manager interface, v3 router, and the periphery immutable state constructor, which requires the factory and the address of weth9 (the ERC-20 wrapper for ether).

Allowing Custody of ERC721 Tokens

To allow the contract to custody ERC721 tokens, implement the onERC721Received function within the inherited IERC721Receiver.sol contract.

The from identifier may be omitted because it is not used.

Creating a Deposit

To add a Deposit instance to the deposits mapping, create an internal function called _createDeposit that destructures the positions struct returned by positions in nonfungiblePositionManager.sol. Pass the relevant variables token0 token1 and liquidity to the deposits mapping.

Uniswap v4 Architecture

Understand the core design pillars of Uniswap v4, including hooks, singleton architecture, and flash accounting.

Uniswap v4 inherits all of the capital efficiency gains of Uniswap v3, but provides flexibility via hooks and gas optimizations across the entire lifecycle.

For additional information, see the Uniswap v4 whitepaper.

Hooks

Developers can attach solidity logic to the swap lifecycle through hooks. The logic executes before and/or after major operations such as pool creation, liquidity addition and removal, swapping, and donations. Hooks are deployed contracts and are called by the Uniswap v4 PoolManager for permissionless execution.

The flexibility of hooks can enable:

  • Limit orders
  • Custom oracles
  • Fee management
  • Automated liquidity management

Dynamic Fees

Uniswap v4 supports dynamic fees, allowing pools to adjust their fees up or down. While other AMMs may have hard-coded logic for dynamic fees, v4 provides no opinionated calculation of the fee. The frequency of liquidity fee updates is also flexible and determined by the developer. Fee updates can occur on every swap, every block, or on an arbitrary schedule (weekly, monthly, yearly, etc).

Dynamic fees open up the design space for fee optimization, value redistribution, and research.

Singleton Design

Architecturally, all pool state and operations are managed by a single contract, PoolManager.sol. The singleton design provides major gas savings. For example, creating a pool is now a state update instead of deploying a new contract. Swapping through multiple pools no longer requires transferring tokens for intermediate pools.

Flash Accounting

By leveraging EIP-1153 transient storage, v4 provides an optimization referred to as flash accounting. Swapping, liquidity modification, and donations incur balance changes, i.e., tokens to be sent in and tokens to be taken out. With flash accounting, these balance changes are efficiently recorded in transient storage and netted against each other. This system allows users to only pay the final balance change, without resolving intermediate balance changes.

Native ETH

Uniswap v4 supports native token assets (Ether), without the need to wrap or unwrap the native token to Wrapped Ether (WETH9).

Custom Accounting

The flexibility of custom accounting allows developers to alter token amounts for swaps and liquidity modifications. The feature opens up the design space for hooks to charge fees or forgo the underlying concentrated liquidity model.

Example use cases:

  • Custom curves, opting out of the concentrated liquidity curve in favor of an independent pricing mechanism
  • Hook swap fees, charging and collecting fees on swaps
  • Liquidity withdrawal fees, penalizing and/or redistributing fee revenue

Core libraries

The PoolManager delegates most of its arithmetic and state handling to a set of libraries in v4-core. These are the contracts a v4 integration reads when reasoning about ticks, prices, deltas and hook permissions.

LibraryWhat it does
TickMathComputes sqrt prices from ticks and vice versa
SqrtPriceMathPrice and amount functions based on Q64.96 sqrt price and liquidity
SwapMathComputes the result of a swap within a single tick
PoolEvery action that can be performed on a pool
PositionPer-position state, keyed by owner and tick range
CurrencyDeltaStores callers' currency deltas in transient storage, the basis of flash accounting
TransientStateLibraryReads the transient state the manager keeps during a lock
ProtocolFeeLibraryPacks and reads the protocol fee for each swap direction
FullMath512-bit multiply and divide without loss of precision
LiquidityMathAdds a signed liquidity delta to liquidity
TickBitmapPacked record of which ticks are initialized

Three libraries have their own pages rather than a row here, because they carry concepts rather than arithmetic: Hooks, LPFeeLibrary and StateLibrary.

Alongside these sit the numeric and encoding helpers: BitMath, FixedPoint96, FixedPoint128, SafeCast, UnsafeMath, CustomRevert, ParseBytes, Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyReserves.

Every library carries natspec on each function, so the source is the reference.

Uniswap v4 Flash Accounting

Understand flash accounting in Uniswap v4 and how deltas reduce transfer overhead.

Flash Accounting

In previous versions of Uniswap, every time a swap was made - including multi-hop swap - tokens were transferred between Pool contracts for intermediate steps.

This design incurred inefficiencies because transferring tokens with external calls to their smart contracts - especially in a multi-hop swap - is quite expensive. This design was required since each pool was its own contract and token transfers were required to maintain accounting and solvency.

With the singleton architecture, a better design was possible and is referred to as Flash Accounting. The design became practical with gas efficiencies of Transient Storage. Flash Accounting further reduces the gas cost of trades that cross multiple pools and supports more complex integrations with Uniswap v4.

With flash accounting, each balance-changing operation (e.g. swap and liquidity modification) updates an internal net balance known as delta. Only the final balance-changes require token transfers.

For example from the above diagrams - let's say you have 20 USDC and 20 USDT but you want to add liquidity with 15 USDC and 25 USDT. Previously this would require multiple external calls as tokens were transferred between Pool contracts when swapping from USDC to USDT. But now with v4's Flash Accounting we only need to keep track of delta - thus we can swap and modifyLiquidity in a single call and only the final balance-changes involve actual token transfers.

In the above example, we are swapping 5 USDC to 5 USDT to create liquidity with 15 USDC and 25 USDT. In between the operations (swap, modifyLiquidity), no token transfers are made

Mechanism

Locking

To ensure correctness and atomicity in complex operations like a multi-hop swap - v4 uses a locking mechanism. Anytime key actions need to take place within the PoolManager - e.g. swaps and liquidity modification - a periphery contract must unlock the PoolManager first. Then integrators implement the unlockCallback and proceed with any of the following actions on the pools:

  • swap
  • modifyLiquidity
  • donate
  • take
  • settle
  • mint
  • burn
  • sync

Note that pool initialization can happen outside the context of unlocking the PoolManager, as there are no balance-changing operations associated with pool creation.

The following diagrams visualize how the above steps will be implemented:

  1. unlock the PoolManager

  2. Implement unlockCallback and proceed with any desired pool actions

  3. The actual token transfer happens at the end and the delta should be resolved

Balance delta

Inside unlockCallback, a periphery contract performs balance-changing operations i.e. conduct swaps, modify positions, etc. After returning execution context back to PoolManager, the core contract checks that balances are resolved - nothing is owed to or from the PoolManager.

The balances resolved above is what we refer as the delta, a field held in the transient state. The value(s) represent the debts and credits of assets owed to or from the PoolManager.

Swapping

As shown in the above diagram, for example - let's say you want to swap ETH for DAI. Assuming this requires a multi-hop swap going from ETH to USDC and then from USDC to DAI.

Previously on v3

  1. ETH is transferred to ETH <> USDC pool contract

  2. USDC is withdrawn from ETH <> USDC contract and transferred to USDC <> DAI contract

  3. DAI is withdrawn from USDC <> DAI contract and transferred to the user

Now on v4

  1. Call swap() on ETH <> USDC

  2. Call swap() on USDC <> DAI, with the credit of USDC from above being used as the input amount

  3. User resolves deltas by paying ETH and receiving DAI

Therefore we can skip the step of actually calling transfer() on the USDC contract.

The optimization scales infinitely, any number of arbitrary hops only requires two token transfers - input and output tokens.

Liquidity Management

The optimization becomes more evident for complex liquidity operations

For example, a user wanted to add liquidity to ETH <> DAI but does not have DAI. The user can swap some ETH to DAI in order to add liquidity with both tokens. In addition, the user can multi-hop swap going from ETH to USDC to DAI. If properly integrated, the user would only need to transfer ETH once.

Fair Combinatorial Batch Auction

CoW Protocol collects and aggregates intents off-chain and auctions them off to solvers. The auction is combinatorial because each solver can submit multiple bids. A solver can submit multiple bids on individual orders, in which case each "bid" represents the best price this solver can provide to an individual order. However, a solver can also submit "batched" bids, that is, bids on groups of orders.

The protocol filters out "unfair" batched bids, which are those delivering less to an order than some available "non-batched" bids. It then selects the combination of winning bids that maximizes the surplus received by the orders that are part of the auction (subject to some computational constraints due to the combinatorial nature of the problem).

The fair combinatorial auction provides several benefits:

  • MEV Protection: Fair combinatorial auctions allow for Uniform Directed Clearing Prices (UDP), where a directed asset pair that appears multiple times across orders in the same auction settles for a consistent price. This makes transaction order irrelevant within the block, undermining the ability for MEV bots to extract value.
  • Coincidence of Wants: When multiple orders trade the same assets within an auction, there may be an opportunity for a peer-to-peer swap that doesn't tap on-chain liquidity, which a solver could exploit by submitting a batched bid.
  • Fairness: Ensuring that each order receives as much as it would have received had that order been auctioned off alone.

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">This contract is the main user-facing contract. Most user interactions with the Aave Protocol occur via the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span> contract. It exposes the liquidity management methods that can be invoked using either <em><strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">Solidity</strong></em> or <em><strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">Web3</strong></em> libraries.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool.sol</span></span></span> allows users to:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Supply</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Withdraw</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Borrow</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Repay</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Enable/disable supplied assets as collateral</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Liquidate positions</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Execute Flash Loans</p></li></ul></div>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Pool is covered by a proxy contract and is owned by the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/pool-addresses-provider"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">PoolAddressesProvider</span></span></span></span></a> of the specific market. All admin functions are callable by the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/pool-configurator"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">PoolConfigurator</span></span></span></span></a> contract defined in the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/pool-addresses-provider"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">PoolAddressesProvider</span></span></span></span></a>.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">The source code is available on <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/protocol/pool/Pool.sol" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline">GitHub</span></a>.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Initializes the Pool.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Function is invoked by the proxy contract when the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span> contract is added to the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/pool-addresses-provider"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">PoolAddressesProvider</span></span></span></span></a> of the market.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Caches the address of the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/pool-addresses-provider"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">PoolAddressesProvider</span></span></span></span></a> in order to reduce gas consumption on subsequent operations.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Supplies a certain <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount</span></span></span> of an <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">asset</span></span></span> into the protocol, minting the same amount of corresponding aTokens and transferring them to the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">onBehalfOf</span></span></span> address. For example, if a user supplies 100 USDC and onBehalfOf address is the same as <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">msg.sender</span></span></span>, they will get 100 aUSDC in return.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">The <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">referralCode</span></span></span> is emitted in Supply event and can be for third-party referral integrations. To activate the referral feature and obtain a unique referral code, integrators need to submit a proposal to Aave Governance.</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-5 knWpsm"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-0 fEZjGH"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-1 hKFRcC"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" style="margin-top:1px"><path d="M9.40192 3.5C10.5566 1.5 13.4434 1.5 14.5981 3.5L20.6603 14C21.815 16 20.3716 18.5 18.0622 18.5H5.93782C3.62842 18.5 2.18505 16 3.33975 14L9.40192 3.5Z" fill="#FFB800" style="fill:color(display-p3 1.0000 0.7216 0.0000)"></path><circle cx="12" cy="14.75" r="1.25" fill="white"></circle><path d="M12 6.5L12 10.5" stroke="white" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"></path></svg></div><p class="sc-c0cf54e3-2 byDogx">When supplying, the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span> contract must have <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">allowance()</span></span></span> to spend funds on
behalf of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">msg.sender</span></span></span> for at least the amount for the asset being supplied.
This can be done via the standard ERC20 <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">approve()</span></span></span> method on the underlying
token contract.</p></div></div>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Withdraws an <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount</span></span></span> of underlying <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">asset</span></span></span> from the reserve, burning the equivalent aTokens owned. <p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If user has any existing debt backed by the underlying token, then the maximum <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount</span></span></span> available to withdraw is the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount</span></span></span> that will not leave user's health factor < 1 after withdrawal.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Repays a borrowed <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount</span></span></span> on a specific reserve, burning the equivalent debt tokens owned. <p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Function to liquidate a non-healthy position collateral-wise, with Health Factor below 1.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">When the health factor of a position is below 1, the caller (liquidator) repays the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">debtToCover</span></span></span> amount of debt of the user getting liquidated. This is part or all of the outstanding borrowed amount on behalf of the borrower. The caller then receives a proportional amount of the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">collateralAsset</span></span></span> (discounted amount of collateral) plus a liquidation bonus to cover market risk.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Liquidators can decide if they want to receive an equivalent amount of collateral aTokens instead of the underlying asset. When the liquidation is completed successfully, the health factor of the position is increased, bringing the health factor above 1.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Liquidators can only close a certain amount of collateral defined by a close factor. Currently the <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">close factor is 0.5</strong>. In other words, liquidators can only liquidate a maximum of 50% of the amount pending to be repaid in a position. The liquidation discount applies to this amount.</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi"><em>In most scenarios</em>, profitable liquidators will choose to liquidate as much as they can (50% of the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">user</span></span></span> position).</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">debtToCover</span></span></span> parameter can be set to <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">uint(-1)</span></span></span> and the protocol will proceed with the highest possible liquidation allowed by the close factor.</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">To check a user's health factor, use [<span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">getUserAccountData()</span></span></span>].</p></li></ul></div>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-5 knWpsm"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-0 itRqXs"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-1 hKFRcC"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="#8F8E8E"></circle><path d="M12 10.3384C12.6904 10.3384 13.25 10.898 13.25 11.5884V16.5884C13.25 17.2787 12.6904 17.8384 12 17.8384C11.3096 17.8384 10.75 17.2787 10.75 16.5884V11.5884C10.75 10.898 11.3096 10.3384 12 10.3384Z" fill="white"></path><circle cx="12" cy="7.41907" r="1.25" fill="white"></circle></svg></div><p class="sc-c0cf54e3-2 byDogx">Liquidators must <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">approve()</span></span></span> the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span> contract to use <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">debtToCover</span></span></span> of the
underlying ERC20 of the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">asset</span></span></span> used for the liquidation.</p></div></div>

The receiver must approve the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span> contract for at least the <em>amount borrowed + fee</em>, otherwise the transaction will revert.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">This function does not waive the fee for approved <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASH_BORROWER</span></span></span>, nor does it allow for opening a debt position instead of repaying.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Updates flash loan premiums. A flash loan premium consists of two parts:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">A part is sent to aToken holders as extra, one time accumulated interest</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">A part is collected by the protocol treasury</p></li></ul></div>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">The total premium is calculated on the total borrowed amount. The premium to protocol is calculated on the total premium, being a percentage of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoanPremiumTotal</span></span></span>.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Configures a new category for the eMode. In eMode, the protocol allows very high borrowing power to borrow assets of the same category. The category 0 is reserved for volatile heterogeneous assets and it's always disabled.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Each eMode category has a custom ltv and liquidation threshold. Each eMode category may or may not have a custom oracle to override the individual assets price oracles.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">The <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/3aad8ca184159732e4b3d8c82cd56a8707a106a2/src/core/contracts/protocol/libraries/types/DataTypes.sol#L105" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline">DataTypes.UserConfigurationMap</span></a> struct is composed of the following fields:</p>
<div style="padding-bottom:48px" data-sticky-first-column="false" class="sc-cfae24d4-0 edshKW"><div class="sc-cfae24d4-1 deBKNp"><div class="sc-bypJrT iqfBFi"><table><thead><tr><th><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz">Name</span></th><th><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz">Type</span></th><th><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz">Description</span></th><th><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz"></span></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz">data</span></td><td><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">uint256</span></span></span></td><td>Bitmap of the users collaterals and borrows. It is divided into pairs of bits, one pair per asset. The first bit indicates if an asset is used as collateral by the user, the second whether an asset is borrowed by the user. The corresponding assets are in the same position as <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">getReservesList()</span></span></span>. For example, if the hex value returned is <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">0x40020</span></span></span>, which represents a decimal value of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">262176</span></span></span>, then in binary it is <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">1000000000000100000</span></span></span>. If we format the binary value into pairs, starting from the right, we get <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">1 00 00 00 00 00 00 10 00 00</span></span></span>. If we start from the right and move left in the above binary pairs, the third pair is <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">10</span></span></span>. Therefore the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">1</span></span></span> indicates that third asset from the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">reserveList</span></span></span> is used as collateral, and <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">0</span></span></span> indicates it has not been borrowed by this user</td><td><span font-size="14" class="sc-aXZVg gJAfGz"></span></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Returns the ongoing normalized income for the reserve.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">A value of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">1e27</span></span></span> means there is no income. As time passes, the yield is accrued. A value of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">2*1e27</span></span></span> means for each unit of asset, one unit of income has been accrued.</p>

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">A value of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">1e27</span></span></span> means there is no debt. Pool
Copy for LLM
This contract is the main user-facing contract. Most user interactions with the Aave Protocol occur via the
Pool
contract. It exposes the liquidity management methods that can be invoked using either
Solidity
or
Web3
libraries.
Pool.sol
allows users to:
Supply
Withdraw
Borrow
Repay
Enable/disable supplied assets as collateral
Liquidate positions
Execute Flash Loans
Pool is covered by a proxy contract and is owned by the
PoolAddressesProvider
of the specific market. All admin functions are callable by the
PoolConfigurator
contract defined in the
PoolAddressesProvider
.
The source code is available on
GitHub
.

Initializes the Pool.
Function is invoked by the proxy contract when the
Pool
contract is added to the
PoolAddressesProvider
of the market.
Caches the address of the
PoolAddressesProvider
in order to reduce gas consumption on subsequent operations.

public
virtual override
Supplies a certain
amount
of an
asset
into the protocol, minting the same amount of corresponding aTokens and transferring them to the
onBehalfOf
address. For example, if a user supplies 100 USDC and onBehalfOf address is the same as
msg.sender
, they will get 100 aUSDC in return.
The
referralCode
is emitted in Supply event and can be for third-party referral integrations. To activate the referral feature and obtain a unique referral code, integrators need to submit a proposal to Aave Governance.
When supplying, the
Pool
contract must have
allowance()
to spend funds on
behalf of
msg.sender
for at least the amount for the asset being supplied.
This can be done via the standard ERC20
approve()
method on the underlying
token contract.
Referral supply is currently inactive, you can pass
0
as
referralCode
.
This program may be activated in the future through an Aave governance
proposal.

Withdraws an
amount
of underlying
asset
from the reserve, burning the equivalent aTokens owned. For example, if a user has 100 aUSDC and calls withdraw(), they will receive 100 USDC, burning the 100 aUSDC.
If user has any existing debt backed by the underlying token, then the maximum
amount
available to withdraw is the
amount
that will not leave user's health factor < 1 after withdrawal.
When withdrawing
to
another address,
msg.sender
should have
aToken
that
will be burned by
Pool
.
Reserves with a Loan To Value parameter of 0% must be disabled as collateral
(using
Pool.setUserUseReserveAsCollateral
or by fully withdrawing the
supplied balance) before other assets can be withdrawn.

,

public
virtual override
Function to liquidate a non-healthy position collateral-wise, with Health Factor below 1.
When the health factor of a position is below 1, the caller (liquidator) repays the
debtToCover
amount of debt of the user getting liquidated. This is part or all of the outstanding borrowed amount on behalf of the borrower. The caller then receives a proportional amount of the
collateralAsset
(discounted amount of collateral) plus a liquidation bonus to cover market risk.
Liquidators can decide if they want to receive an equivalent amount of collateral aTokens instead of the underlying asset. When the liquidation is completed successfully, the health factor of the position is increased, bringing the health factor above 1.
Liquidators can only close a certain amount of collateral defined by a close factor. Currently the
close factor is 0.5
. In other words, liquidators can only liquidate a maximum of 50% of the amount pending to be repaid in a position. The liquidation discount applies to this amount.
In most scenarios
, profitable liquidators will choose to liquidate as much as they can (50% of the
user
position).
debtToCover
parameter can be set to
uint(-1)
and the protocol will proceed with the highest possible liquidation allowed by the close factor.
To check a user's health factor, use [
getUserAccountData()
].
Liquidators must
approve()
the
Pool
contract to use
debtToCover
of the
underlying ERC20 of the
asset
used for the liquidation.

<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Flash Loans are special transactions that allow the borrowing of an asset, as long as the borrowed amount (and a fee) is returned before the end of the transaction (also called One Block Borrows). These transactions do not require a user to supply collateral prior to engaging in the transaction. There is no real world analogy to Flash Loans, so it requires some basic understanding of how state is managed within blocks in blockchains.</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-5 knWpsm"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-0 itRqXs"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-1 hKFRcC"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="#8F8E8E"></circle><path d="M12 10.3384C12.6904 10.3384 13.25 10.898 13.25 11.5884V16.5884C13.25 17.2787 12.6904 17.8384 12 17.8384C11.3096 17.8384 10.75 17.2787 10.75 16.5884V11.5884C10.75 10.898 11.3096 10.3384 12 10.3384Z" fill="white"></path><circle cx="12" cy="7.41907" r="1.25" fill="white"></circle></svg></div><p class="sc-c0cf54e3-2 byDogx">Flash Loans are an advanced concept aimed at developers. You must have a good
understanding of EVM, programming, and smart contracts to be able to use this
feature.</p></div></div>
<section id="overview" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h2 font-size="20" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg cqzZa-D">Overview</h2></div><a href="#overview" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Flash-loan allows users to access liquidity of the pool (only for reserves for which borrow is enabled) for one transaction as long as the amount taken plus fee is returned or (if allowed) debt position is opened by the end of the transaction.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Aave v3 offers two options for flash loans:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi"><a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloan"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoan()</span></span></span></span></a>: Allows borrower to access liquidity of <em><strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">multiple reserves</strong></em> in single <em>flashLoan</em> transaction. The borrower also has an option to open variable rate borrow position backed by supplied collateral or credit delegation in this case.<br/>
<!-- -->NOTE: <em>flash loan fee</em> is waived for approved <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashBorrowers</span></span></span> (managed by <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/acl-manager"><span class="underline">ACLManager</span></a>)</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi"><a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloansimple"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoanSimple()</span></span></span></span></a>: Allows borrower to access liquidity of <em>single reserve</em> for the transaction. In this case flash loan fee is not waived nor can borrower open any debt position at the end of the transaction. This method is gas efficient for those trying take advantage of simple flash loan with single reserve asset.</p></li></ul></div>
<section id="overview-execution-flow" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">Execution Flow</h3></div><a href="#overview-execution-flow" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">For developers, a helpful mental model to consider when developing your solution:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ol class="sc-311ed6a9-0 junwhx"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Your contract calls the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a> contract, requesting a Flash Loan of a certain <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount(s)</span></span></span> of <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">reserve(s)</span></span></span> using <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloansimple"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoanSimple()</span></span></span></span></a> or <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloan"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoan()</span></span></span></span></a>.</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">After some sanity checks, the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a> transfers the requested <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amounts</span></span></span> of the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">reserves</span></span></span> to your contract, then calls <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">executeOperation()</span></span></span> on <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">receiver</span></span></span> contract .</p></li><li>Your contract, now holding the flash loaned <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amount(s)</span></span></span>, executes any arbitrary operation in its code. <!-- -->
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If you are performing a <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">flashLoanSimple</strong>, then when your code has finished, you approve Pool for flash loaned amount + fee.</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If you are performing <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">flashLoan,</strong> then for all the reserves either depending on <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">interestRateMode</span></span></span> passed for the asset, either the Pool must be approved for flash loaned amount + fee or must or sufficient collateral or credit delegation should be available to open debt position.</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If the amount owed is not available (due to a lack of balance or approval or insufficient collateral for debt), then the transaction is reverted.</p></li></ul></div>
</li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">All of the above happens in 1 transaction (hence in a single ethereum block).</p></li></ol></div>
<section id="overview-applications-of-flash-loans" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">Applications of Flash Loans</h3></div><a href="#overview-applications-of-flash-loans" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Aave Flash Loans are already used with Aave v3 for liquidity switch feature. Other examples in the wild include:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Arbitrage between assets, without needing to have the principal amount to execute the arbitrage.</p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Liquidating borrow positions, without having to repay the debt of the positions and using discounted collateral claimed to payoff flashLoan amount + fee.</p></li></ul></div>
<section id="overview-flash-loan-fee" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">Flash loan fee</h3></div><a href="#overview-flash-loan-fee" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">The flash loan fee is initialized at deployment to 0.05% and can be updated via Governance Vote. Use <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_total"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL</span></span></span></span></a> to get current value.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Flashloan fee can be shared by the LPs (liquidity providers) and the protocol treasury. The <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_total"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL</span></span></span></span></a> represents the total fee paid by the borrowers of which:</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Fee to LP: <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_total"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL</span></span></span></span></a> - <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_to_protocol"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TO_PROTOCOL</span></span></span></span></a></p></li><li><p class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Fee to Protocol: <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_to_protocol"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TO_PROTOCOL</span></span></span></span></a></p></li></ul></div>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-5 knWpsm"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-0 itRqXs"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-1 hKFRcC"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="#8F8E8E"></circle><path d="M12 10.3384C12.6904 10.3384 13.25 10.898 13.25 11.5884V16.5884C13.25 17.2787 12.6904 17.8384 12 17.8384C11.3096 17.8384 10.75 17.2787 10.75 16.5884V11.5884C10.75 10.898 11.3096 10.3384 12 10.3384Z" fill="white"></path><circle cx="12" cy="7.41907" r="1.25" fill="white"></circle></svg></div><p class="sc-c0cf54e3-2 byDogx">At initialization,
<a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#view-methods-flashloan_premium_to_protocol"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TO_PROTOCOL</span></span></span></span></a>
is set to 0.</p></div></div>
<section id="step-by-step" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h2 font-size="20" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg cqzZa-D">Step by step</h2></div><a href="#step-by-step" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<section id="step-by-step-section-1-setting-up" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">1. Setting Up</h3></div><a href="#step-by-step-section-1-setting-up" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Your contract that receives the flash loaned amounts <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">must</strong> conform to the <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/misc/flashloan/interfaces/IFlashLoanSimpleReceiver.sol" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">IFlashLoanSimpleReceiver</span></span></span></span></a> or <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/misc/flashloan/interfaces/IFlashLoanReceiver.sol" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">IFlashLoanReceiver</span></span></span></span></a> interface by implementing the relevant <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">executeOperation()</span></span></span> function.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Also note that since the owed amounts will be <em>pulled</em> from your contract, your contract must give allowance to the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a> to pull those funds to pay back the flash loan amount + premiums.</p>
<section id="step-by-step-section-2-calling-flashloan-or-flashloansimple" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">2. Calling flashLoan() or flashLoanSimple()</h3></div><a href="#step-by-step-section-2-calling-flashloan-or-flashloansimple" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">To call either of the two flash loan methods on the Pool, we need to pass in the relevant parameters. There are 3 ways you can do this.</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ol class="sc-311ed6a9-0 junwhx"><li>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">From an EOA ('normal' ethereum account)</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">To use an EOA, send a transaction to the relevant <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a> calling the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloan"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoan()</span></span></span></span></a> or <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloansimple"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoanSimple()</span></span></span></span></a> function. See the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a> docs for parameter details, ensuring you use your contract address from <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/flash-loans#1-setting-up"><span class="underline">step 1</span></a> for the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">receiverAddress</span></span></span>.</p>
</li><li>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">From a different contract</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Similar to sending a transaction from an EOA as above, ensure the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">receiverAddress</span></span></span> is your contract address from <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/flash-loans#1-setting-up"><span class="underline">step 1</span></a>.</p>
</li><li>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">From the <em>same</em> contract</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If you want to use the same contract as in step 1, use <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">address(this)</span></span></span> for the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">receiverAddress</span></span></span> parameter in the flash loan method.</p>
</li></ol></div>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-5 knWpsm"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-0 fEZjGH"><div class="sc-c0cf54e3-1 hKFRcC"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" style="margin-top:1px"><path d="M9.40192 3.5C10.5566 1.5 13.4434 1.5 14.5981 3.5L20.6603 14C21.815 16 20.3716 18.5 18.0622 18.5H5.93782C3.62842 18.5 2.18505 16 3.33975 14L9.40192 3.5Z" fill="#FFB800" style="fill:color(display-p3 1.0000 0.7216 0.0000)"></path><circle cx="12" cy="14.75" r="1.25" fill="white"></circle><path d="M12 6.5L12 10.5" stroke="white" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"></path></svg></div><p class="sc-c0cf54e3-2 byDogx">Never keep funds permanently on your
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/misc/flashloan/base/FlashLoanReceiverBase.sol" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">FlashLoanReceiverBase</span></span></span></span></a>
contract as they could be exposed to a <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/a/92457/19365" class="sc-a2775aab-4 bPPxQN"><span class="underline">'griefing'
attack</span></a>, where the stored
funds are used by an attacker.</p></div></div>
<section id="step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h3 font-size="16" font-weight="600" class="sc-aXZVg gLzrMZ">Completing the flash loan</h3></div><a href="#step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Once you have performed your logic with the flash loaned assets (in your <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">executeOperation()</span></span></span> function), you will need to pay back the flash loaned amounts if you used <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloansimple"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoanSimple()</span></span></span></span></a> or <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">interestRateModes = 0</span></span></span> in <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool#write-methods-flashloan"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">flashLoan()</span></span></span></span></a> for any of the assets in <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">modes</span></span></span> parameter.</p>
<div class="sc-a2775aab-0 bcLawT"><ul class="sc-311ed6a9-0 jBMvqz"><li>
<section id="step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan-paying-back-a-flash-loaned-asset" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h4 font-size="16" font-weight="500" class="sc-aXZVg ixFGtv">Paying back a flash loaned asset</h4></div><a href="#step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan-paying-back-a-flash-loaned-asset" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">Ensure your contract has the relevant amount + premium to payback the borrowed asset. You can calculate this by taking the sum of the relevant entry in the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">amounts</span></span></span> and <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">premiums</span></span></span> array passed into the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">executeOperation()</span></span></span> function.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">You <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">do not</strong> need to transfer the owed amount back to the <a class="sc-a2775aab-3 bDBKtw" href="/docs/aave-v3/guides/smart-contracts/pool"><span class="underline"><span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">Pool</span></span></span></span></a>. The funds will be automatically <em>pulled</em> at the conclusion of your operation.</p>
</li><li>
<section id="step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan-incurring-a-debt-ie-not-immediately-paying-back" class="sc-7b805187-1 bvRaHC"><div class="sc-gEvEer fDzIsf"><h4 font-size="16" font-weight="500" class="sc-aXZVg ixFGtv">Incurring a debt (i.e. not immediately paying back)</h4></div><a href="#step-by-step-completing-the-flash-loan-incurring-a-debt-ie-not-immediately-paying-back" class="sc-7b805187-0 hvvfME"><svg width="13" height="14" viewBox="0 0 13 14" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5.39979 3.91466L6.55689 2.75757C6.81014 2.50431 7.1108 2.30342 7.44169 2.16636C7.77258 2.0293 8.12723 1.95876 8.48538 1.95876C8.84354 1.95876 9.19819 2.0293 9.52908 2.16636C9.85997 2.30342 10.1606 2.50431 10.4139 2.75757C10.6671 3.01082 10.868 3.31148 11.0051 3.64237C11.1421 3.97326 11.2127 4.32791 11.2127 4.68606C11.2127 5.04422 11.1421 5.39887 11.0051 5.72976C10.868 6.06065 10.6671 6.36131 10.4139 6.61456L9.25678 7.77166M6.94259 10.0859L5.78549 11.243C5.53224 11.4962 5.23158 11.6971 4.90069 11.8342C4.5698 11.9712 4.21515 12.0418 3.85699 12.0418C3.13367 12.0418 2.43997 11.7544 1.9285 11.2429C1.41703 10.7315 1.12969 10.0378 1.12969 9.31445C1.12969 8.59113 1.41703 7.89743 1.9285 7.38596L3.08559 6.22886" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path><path d="M4.62842 8.54297L7.71401 5.45737" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></section>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">If you initially used a <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">mode=1</span></span></span> or <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">mode=2</span></span></span> for any of the assets in the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">modes</span></span></span> parameter, then the address passed in for <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">onBehalfOf</span></span></span> will incur the debt <strong style="font-weight:500;color:#1A1A1A">if</strong> the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">onBehalfOf</span></span></span> address has previously approved the <span class="sc-5705a70a-0 guTZxP code"><span class="sc-hHOBiw kGGtlD"><span class="sc-aXZVg brTrVz">msg.sender</span></span></span> to incur debts on their behalf.</p>
<p data-paragraph="true" class="sc-a2775aab-6 cFAMWi">This means that you can have some assets that are paid back immediately, while other assets incur a debt.</p>
